high_consensus.description: This is a real reliability gap. Moving endpoints without explicitly defining retry, timeout, backoff, and 429/5xx handling leaves production behavior ambiguous and untestable. Low-to-moderate implementation cost, high operational impact.

Strong and actionable. One-time migrations are high-risk failure points; idempotency, ordering, validation, and partial-failure handling should be explicit in acceptance criteria. High ROI for Sprint 1 safety.
Important incident-response ambiguity. Kill-switch versus user pin precedence must be deterministic and documented, otherwise operators cannot reliably mitigate risk during outages or regressions.
Strong improvement. Cost-cap behavior is safety-critical; undefined mid-cycle handling can cause partial-state failures. Per-workflow failure/recovery contract should be explicit and testable.

blockers.concern: Cost cap requirement is underspecified (session boundary, parallel workers, shared ledger consistency).
blockers.why_matters: A per-session cap can be bypassed or enforced inconsistently in concurrent runs, leading to unexpected spend despite apparent guardrails.
blockers.recommendation: Define canonical session ID, ledger isolation rules, concurrency-safe accounting, and behavior for distributed/multi-process execution.

blockers.concern: Gemini fallback demotion lacks hysteresis/cooldown semantics and may thrash between primary and fallback.
blockers.why_matters: Probe state flapping can cause non-deterministic model routing between calls, making outputs inconsistent and debugging nearly impossible.
blockers.recommendation: Define fallback state machine with cooldown window, minimum healthy probes before restore, and sticky session behavior.

blockers.concern: Kill-switch behavior is internally contradictory (alias rollback vs endpoint forcing).
blockers.why_matters: The PRD states the kill-switch must operate at alias resolution only, but FR-1 test criteria also says it should force /chat/completions for gpt-5.5. If implemented incorrectly, incident rollback will create guaranteed 400 failures for gpt-5.5 traffic.
blockers.location: FR-1 Acceptance Criteria; Risks & Mitigation (kill-switch notes)
blockers.recommendation: Resolve to one contract: alias-level rollback only. Remove endpoint-force language and add explicit negative test asserting kill-switch does NOT alter endpoint routing logic.

blockers.concern: SSOT-to-generated-map synchronization is not transactionally enforced, risking runtime drift between Python and bash call paths.
blockers.why_matters: If model-config.yaml changes land without regenerated maps (or vice versa), different execution paths can resolve models/costs differently, causing hard-to-diagnose production bugs.
blockers.location: FR-2 Acceptance Criteria (map regeneration); Technical Constraints (Bash + Python consume SSOT)
blockers.recommendation: Make map generation a mandatory CI gate with checksum verification and fail merges when generated artifacts are stale.

blockers.concern: Unknown /v1/responses output shapes are configured to hard-fail, creating outage risk on provider contract evolution.
blockers.why_matters: OpenAI can introduce new block types; immediate UnsupportedResponseShapeError would break production flows even when a usable text answer exists.
blockers.location: Scope (unknown future object types); Technical Considerations §3.1
blockers.recommendation: Add forward-compatible parsing: preserve known blocks, ignore unknown non-critical blocks with WARN telemetry, and fail only when no valid content can be extracted.

blockers.concern: Using rolling model aliases as production defaults without a canary strategy creates uncontrolled behavior drift.
blockers.why_matters: Provider-side behavior can change without code changes. A sudden model update could impact quality, latency, safety, or cost across all users simultaneously.
blockers.recommendation: Add staged rollout requirements: canary cohort, percentage-based rollout, and automatic rollback thresholds for error/cost/latency regressions.
